text:
24-hour news summary.

1 DeformX demonstrates a robot using a simulation-trained policy to whip a rope and knock an apple from someone’s head, modeling flexible cables with Cosserat rod physics and NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

2 NVIDIA introduced its Open Agent Safety Platform, combining OpenShell and Sentry with more than 100 industry partners to build an open trust and safety layer for AI agents.

3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5521) The linked X post is no longer available.

4 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5522) In an AI bridge-design contest, Claude Opus 5.5 won decisively by supporting an estimated 130 pounds while using the least printing time, parts, and filament.

5 Meta reportedly hired MongoDB CEO CJ Desai to lead its enterprise AI efforts, shortly before he would have qualified for most of a large equity grant.

6 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5524) ElevenLabs launched Eleven v4 and v4 Turbo, describing them as its fastest and most expressive voice models and reporting a top ranking from Artificial Analysis.

7 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5525) Dyna Robotics previewed a new robot designed for detailed, demanding real-world work, with more information promised soon.

8 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5526) Hugging Face’s Clem described an OpenShell contribution that detects malicious agent coordination through allowed network destinations by monitoring traffic budgets, behavioral drift, and fleet-wide anomalies.

9 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5527) Manus introduced personal agents on its Cue platform.

10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5528) Mo launched as an AI QA engineer that deploys more than 100 agents to test apps in parallel, claiming more bugs found, faster discovery, and lower cost than Codex with Playwright MCP.

11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5529) Fo launched a personal AI service that combines agents with human assistance, claiming twice the real-world task completion and a 94% trust rate.

12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5530) Anthropic announced Claude Sonnet 5.5 as a faster, cheaper complement to Opus 5.5 for everyday tasks, coding fixes, and polished office documents.

13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5531) Artificial Analysis reported that Claude Sonnet 5.5 ranks second on its Intelligence Index, matching leading models on several tasks but using substantially more output tokens and costing more per task.

14 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5532) WonderSearch launched a query-time search system for millions of unstructured documents that avoids corpus-wide embeddings and vector-index maintenance.

15 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5533) An MIT essay argues that AI’s rapid progress does not diminish the value of an AI PhD, emphasizing public contributions, deep expertise, human judgment, and pursuing important research questions.

16 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5534) David George shared an article arguing that OpenAI’s unusual strength is repeatedly discovering simple, transformative product primitives and building them into a broad platform.

17 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5535) AMD announced that World Labs and Fei-Fei Li are joining the company to combine spatial-intelligence and world-model expertise with AMD’s computing capabilities.

18 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5536) A technology analyst predicted that OpenAI will soon reveal its always-on agent, reportedly called “o” or “Aeon,” while suggesting GPT-6 Astra may also receive an update.

19 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5537) CBC reported that Mother Jones reviewed extensive ChatGPT conversations allegedly used by the Tumbler Ridge shooter to plan the attack and evade OpenAI’s safety safeguards.

20 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5538) Supertake launched a platform that uses frontier AI and trading agents to turn users’ views into shareable investment portfolios.

--Hermes
